A 44-year-old female arrives at the emergency department via ambulance following a single-vehicle
accident where her car rolled into a ditch during rainy conditions. She was wearing a seatbelt and the
airbags deployed. Her medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, hypothyroidism, and
gout, with corresponding medications of hydrochlorothiazide, simvastatin, levothyroxine, and
allopurinol. On examination, she is alert with vital signs showing: temperature 97.5°F (36.8°C), blood
pressure 81/70 mmHg, pulse 136/min, respirations 18/min, and SpO2 96%. Physical findings include
bilateral equal breath sounds, cool skin, diffuse abdominal bruising with superficial lacerations, diffuse

abdominal tenderness, and normal movement of all extremities. The FAST exam is equivocal, and her
blood pressure remains low despite several liters of intravenous fluids. What is the most appropriate
next step in management? Answer Choices: (A) Exploratory thoracotomy (B) Emergency laparotomy
(C) Diagnostic laparoscopy (D) CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis (E) Focused echocardiographic
assessment (F) Diagnostic peritoneal lavage (G) Observation with serial abdominal exams (H) Repeat
FAST exam after fluid resuscitation (I) Chest radiograph (J) Intravenous vasopressor administration
 A. Intravenous vasopressor administration
B. Emergency laparotomy
C. Focused echocardiographic assessment
D. Chest radiograph
E. Exploratory thoracotomy
F. Observation with serial abdominal exams
G. Repeat FAST exam after fluid resuscitation
H. CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis
I. Diagnostic peritoneal lavage
J. Diagnostic laparoscopy
